paragraphs.title: A Request for Compassion, Protection, and Salvation

answers: The LORD
His enemies
The nations
easy.explanation: He calls upon the LORD, asking Him to bow down His ear and hear him.
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist appeal for help?

answers: Rich and powerful
Poor and needy
A ruler over nations
easy.explanation: He says, “I am poor and needy.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe his condition?

answers: Rejoice it
Hide it
Cast it away
easy.explanation: He asks, “Rejoice the soul of thy servant.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do to his soul?

answers: Because he is holy and trusts in God
Because he wants to become a king
Because all nations fear him
medium.explanation: He says, “Preserve my soul; for I am holy,” and describes himself as God’s servant who trusts in Him.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD to preserve his soul?

answers: He lifts it up unto the LORD
He hides it from his enemies
He gives it to the nations
medium.explanation: He says, “unto thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist say he does with his soul?

answers: Set apart or devoted to God
A powerful enemy
A person who never prays
medium.explanation: In this context, the psalmist presents himself as devoted or faithful to God.
medium.q: What does “holy” mean in the phrase “for I am holy”?

answers: Hearing, preservation, mercy, salvation, and joy
Judgment, punishment, war, and victory
Wealth, honor, rule, and fame
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks God to hear him, preserve him, show mercy, save him, and rejoice his soul.
challenge.q: Which sequence of requests appears in verses 1–4?

answers: The psalmist is vulnerable but relies upon God
The psalmist needs no help from God
The psalmist considers himself God’s enemy
challenge.explanation: Although he is in a needy condition, his trust in God gives him hope and support.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the combination of “poor and needy” and “trusteth in thee”?

answers: Dependence and confidence in God during trouble
A desire to avoid God
Indifference to his situation
challenge.explanation: He repeatedly turns to the LORD because he sees Him as the source of help and salvation.
challenge.q: What does the repeated appeal to the LORD reveal about the psalmist?

paragraphs.title: God’s Goodness and Response to Prayer

answers: Goodness, forgiveness, and abundant mercy
Harshness, distance, and anger
Weakness, sorrow, and silence
easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD is good, ready to forgive, and plenteous in mercy.
easy.q: What qualities of the LORD are mentioned in verse 5?

answers: All who call upon Him
Kings only
His enemies only
easy.explanation: The verse says His mercy is “unto all them that call upon thee.”
easy.q: To whom is the LORD’s mercy extended?

answers: In the day of his trouble
Only on a day of joy
After his enemies defeat him
easy.explanation: He says, “In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee.”
easy.q: When does the psalmist say he will call upon the LORD?

answers: Because he relies on God’s goodness, forgiveness, and mercy
Because he believes God cannot hear
Because he wants to conceal his trouble
medium.explanation: His request rests on his confidence that the LORD is good, forgiving, and merciful.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD to listen to his prayer?

answers: He will call upon God in trouble because God will answer him
He will remain silent because God will not answer
He will call upon the nations to receive an answer
medium.explanation: He declares that he will call upon the LORD because he knows that God will answer him.
medium.q: What connection does the psalmist make between trouble and God’s answer?

answers: Humble prayers and earnest requests
Songs of military victory
Commands given to enemies
medium.explanation: Supplications are earnest, humble prayers or pleas for help.
medium.q: What does “supplications” mean in “the voice of my supplications”?

answers: Because the LORD is good and forgiving, the psalmist calls upon Him expecting an answer
Because the LORD is distant, the psalmist stops praying
Because the enemies are good, the psalmist asks them for help
challenge.explanation: God’s goodness and mercy provide the basis for the psalmist’s prayer and confidence that God will answer.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in verses 5–7?

answers: It is presented as available to all who call upon Him
It is reserved for the psalmist alone
It is given only to those who are not troubled
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that God’s abundant mercy is extended to all who call upon Him.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “all them that call upon thee” show about God’s mercy?

answers: He prays persistently and trusts that God will answer
He prays only once without hope
He prefers not to call upon God
challenge.explanation: He asks God to hear him and promises to call in the day of trouble, confident that God will answer.
challenge.q: How is the psalmist’s attitude toward prayer described in these verses?

paragraphs.title: God’s Uniqueness and Honor Among the Nations

answers: There is none like Him
He is one of many equal gods
He is weaker than the others
easy.explanation: He says, “Among the gods there is none like unto thee, O Lord.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe the LORD among the gods?

answers: Come and worship before the LORD
Disappear from the earth
Fight one another before the LORD
easy.explanation: The verse says that all nations God has made shall come and worship before Him.
easy.q: What will all nations do according to verse 9?

answers: Because He is great and does wondrous things
Because He seeks wealth
Because He is one of the nations
easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “thou art great, and doest wondrous things.”
easy.q: Why is the LORD worthy of honor?

answers: Because He alone is God, the nations will worship and glorify His name
Because He needs the nations, they will rule over Him
Because He is equal to humans, they will not honor Him
medium.explanation: God’s unique greatness leads the nations to worship Him and glorify His name.
medium.q: What connection is made between God’s uniqueness and His honor among the nations?

answers: No works compare with God’s works
God has done no works
Human works are greater than God’s works
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that God’s deeds are incomparable.
medium.q: What does the phrase “neither are there any works like unto thy works” mean?

answers: No one compares with God; the nations will honor Him; He is great and does wonders
The nations fight; the psalmist gives thanks; God hides Himself
God asks for help; the nations refuse; the psalmist is silent
medium.explanation: The passage moves from God’s uniqueness to the nations’ worship and then to His greatness and wondrous works.
medium.q: Which order of ideas appears in verses 8–10?

answers: All nations are presented as creatures made by God
The nations have no connection with God
Only one nation is described as made by God
challenge.explanation: By calling them nations whom God has made, the verse connects all peoples with God as their Creator.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the phrase “all nations whom thou hast made”?

answers: It reinforces God’s uniqueness and exclusive deity
It presents God as part of a group
It removes the importance of His wonders
challenge.explanation: The phrase summarizes and intensifies the claim that God alone is God.
challenge.q: How does “thou art God alone” strengthen the main idea?

answers: God’s greatness and wonders lead the nations to worship and glorify Him
God’s greatness causes the nations to ignore Him
The nations worship only because the psalmist commands them
challenge.explanation: The passage presents God’s greatness and wondrous works as the reason for the nations’ recognition and worship.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between God’s greatness and the nations’ action?

paragraphs.title: Guidance, an Undivided Heart, and Gratitude

answers: His way
The ways of his enemies
The names of the nations
easy.explanation: He asks, “Teach me thy way, O LORD.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to teach him?

answers: God’s truth
The way of his enemies
The way of wealth
easy.explanation: He says, “I will walk in thy truth.”
easy.q: In what does the psalmist say he will walk?

answers: With all his heart
Only with his lips
Only before his enemies
easy.explanation: He says, “I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with all my heart.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist promise to praise the LORD?

answers: Learning God’s way leads the psalmist to live according to His truth
Learning God’s way causes him to leave the truth
The two ideas are unrelated
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks to be taught God’s way so that he may walk in God’s truth.
medium.q: What is the connection between learning God’s way and walking in His truth?

answers: To direct his whole heart toward reverence for God
To divide his heart away from faith
To hide his heart from other people
medium.explanation: He asks for an undivided heart wholly directed toward reverence for God’s name.
medium.q: What does “unite my heart to fear thy name” mean in context?

answers: Because of God’s great mercy and His deliverance of his soul
Because he wants to become one of the nations
Because his enemies praised him
medium.explanation: He remembers God’s great mercy and that God delivered his soul from the lowest hell.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist praise and glorify the LORD?

answers: The psalmist moves from asking for guidance and an undivided heart to promising praise because of God’s mercy and deliverance
He moves from thanking God for deliverance to asking for wealth
He moves from describing enemies to describing the nations
challenge.explanation: He first asks for guidance and a united heart, then commits himself to praise in response to God’s mercy and rescue.
challenge.q: What movement of thought occurs between verses 11 and 13?

answers: His praise is intended to be wholehearted and lasting
His praise will be partial and temporary
He does not truly intend to praise God
challenge.explanation: The phrases emphasize both the completeness and the continuing nature of his praise.
challenge.q: What does the combination of “with all my heart” and “for evermore” suggest?

answers: Great mercy and deliverance contrasted with the lowest hell
Wealth contrasted with honor
Peace among nations contrasted with joy of soul
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts God’s great mercy and rescue with the depth of danger represented by the lowest hell.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in verse 13?

paragraphs.title: Rescue from Enemies and a Sign of Goodness

answers: The proud and assemblies of violent men
The holy and those who call upon God
All the nations that worship God
easy.explanation: He describes the proud and violent men who have sought after his soul.
easy.q: Who has risen against the psalmist?

answers: Compassionate, gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth
Proud and violent
Weak and distant
easy.explanation: These are the qualities he attributes to the LORD in verse 15.
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe the LORD?

answers: A token for good
A hidden name
The psalmist’s enemies’ strength
easy.explanation: He asks, “Show me a token for good.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to show him?

answers: The enemies seek his life, while the LORD is compassionate, gracious, and merciful
The enemies are compassionate, while the LORD seeks his life
There is no difference between the enemies and the LORD
medium.explanation: The psalmist contrasts the violence of his enemies with the compassion and mercy of God.
medium.q: What contrast appears between the enemies and the LORD in verses 14–15?

answers: Strength, salvation, and a token for good
Wealth, authority, and fame
Silence, concealment, and escape
medium.explanation: He asks God to give strength to His servant, save him, and show him a token for good.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask for after asking the LORD to turn toward him?

answers: Patient and slow to anger
Quick to become angry
Unable to give help
medium.explanation: Longsuffering describes patience and a refusal to become angry quickly.

answers: So that his enemies may see God’s help and be ashamed
So that his enemies may become stronger against him
So that he may hide God’s help from his enemies
challenge.explanation: He asks for a sign so that those who hate him may see that the LORD has helped and comforted him and may be ashamed.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the token for good at the end of the psalm?

answers: The psalmist asks for God’s attention and mercy, strength, salvation, and then a token for good
He praises the nations, asks for wealth, and then becomes silent
He gives thanks, turns away, and abandons hope of salvation
challenge.explanation: The requests progress from God’s attention and mercy to strength, salvation, and visible confirmation of God’s goodness.
challenge.q: How does the sequence of requests develop in verses 16–17?

answers: The psalmist presents himself as belonging to God’s household and asks for His salvation
The psalmist declares himself to be God’s enemy
The psalmist asks the nations alone for help
challenge.explanation: The expression identifies the psalmist as God’s servant and supports his appeal for God to save him.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the expression “the son of thine handmaid”?
